assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned a superconducting circuit into a controllable atom-photon system with strong coupling, dispersive readout and photon-mediated qubit coupling. It underlies essentially all present superconducting quantum processors and microwave quantum optics. The idea is clear, original and has had large lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: The theory proposal (Blais, Girvin, Schoelkopf and colleagues) and the Yale experiments are the core. Credit is shared with other leaders, notably Wallraff, who is not among the supplied names, so the supplied triple is a fair but incomplete configuration. I have close professional familiarity with this area, which I try to separate from the merits.
assessment.maturity: Strong coupling was reproduced by many groups over two decades and the framework is textbook-stable. Recognition is timely, with some risk that it overlaps conceptually with the recent circuit-quantum-tunnelling prize.
uncertainties: Whether the credited names omit decisive contributors such as Wallraff.
Degree of overlap with the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize.
Whether the committee would see this as a distinct discovery or a continuation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices created clean, tunable quantum simulators of Hubbard-type many-body physics, including the superfluid to Mott insulator transition, and now probe single-site resolved correlations. The conceptual and experimental impact across condensed matter and quantum information is broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch/Cirac supplied the theoretical proposals; Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger delivered the key experiments. Five names are credited and the prize allows only three, so any triple omits important contributors. Zoller, Bloch, Greiner is a defensible compromise between theory and experiment.
assessment.maturity: The Mott transition and subsequent quantum gas microscopy are well confirmed by independent groups. The field is mature, and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Which of Cirac, Esslinger and Jaksch (not listed) should be recognized over the chosen three.
Overlap with earlier cold-atom prizes (BEC, laser cooling).
Whether quantum simulation is judged a discovery or a method.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter, a new tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. It is original and has generated a very large field.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery in 2018. Cao and others on the experiment are not among the supplied names; the theory-plus-experiment triple is clean.
assessment.maturity: The core experiments have been reproduced widely, but the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still debated. Recognition is perhaps early, though impact is clear.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the interpretation of correlated phases remain unsettled.
Whether other theorists or experimental co-first authors deserve mention.
Possible prematurity compared with more settled candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction and the threshold theorem show that large quantum computations are possible despite noise, and the surface code defines the architecture most experimental groups pursue. The idea is foundational and, as someone who works toward fault-tolerant processors, I find the experimental relevance very high.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane introduced the first codes, Kitaev topological codes and fault tolerance. Others (Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme, Aharonov, Ben-Or, Preskill) contributed decisively, so any three is a contestable cut.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations of below-threshold logical error rates have appeared only recently, so confirmation is strong in theory but still developing in practice. There is also a question of whether this is physics or computer science and mathematics.
uncertainties: Fit with the physics prize remit.
Large number of deserving contributors beyond three.
Full-scale fault tolerance not yet demonstrated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal for electron spins in quantum dots as qubits and its realization with single-spin control and readout, and later with silicon devices, established a major platform for scalable semiconductor quantum computing. It is clear, original and of growing significance.
assessment.attribution: Loss and DiVincenzo made the 1998 proposal; Vandersypen and others (Kouwenhoven, Petta/Yacoby, Tarucha) provided experimental realization. The supplied triple is reasonable but leaves out other key experimentalists.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation by multiple groups, including high-fidelity silicon two-qubit gates, is solid. Whether the platform will win out is unknown, which affects timing.
uncertainties: Competing experimental credit among several groups.
Technological winner among qubit platforms is undecided.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect introduced a new class of quantum matter with protected edge states, with broad influence on condensed matter and potentially on topological quantum devices. The concept is original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental demonstration in HgTe. Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and others contributed to the HgTe prediction, which complicates attribution, and Zhang is deceased.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by independent ARPES and transport work, and mature. Recognition is timely or somewhat overdue, but the 2016 topology prize already covers adjacent ground.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize on topological phase transitions.
Credit for the HgTe prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum light-matter interfaces, including cavity QED quantum networks, atomic-ensemble memories and photon-atom gates, provide the basis for quantum repeaters and distributed quantum information. The contributions are important, though the topic is a compound of several strands.
assessment.attribution: Kimble, Rempe and Lukin each made decisive and distinct contributions, but they span different approaches, so the discovery is somewhat compound and unification is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Elements are well confirmed in many laboratories, while full quantum networks over long distances are still developing. Recognition is plausible but arguably early.
uncertainties: Compound discovery with distinct parts.
Practical quantum network demonstrations remain limited.
Credit for ensemble memories also involves other groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reaching 10^-18 fractional uncertainty rely on the magic-wavelength concept and enable tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. Impact is large and the concept is clear.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock; Ye's group demonstrated record accuracy and stability. A two-person configuration is clean, though other clock groups (for example ion-clock groups) also contribute to the broader field.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several independent institutions, though the redefinition of the second has not yet happened. Timing is reasonable, but there is some overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes in precision spectroscopy and ion control.
uncertainties: Overlap with previous precision-measurement prizes.
Competition with ion-clock results for credit.
